problem: Prior robot memory systems (caption-based databases like ReMEmbR, semantic forests like Embodied-RAG, scene graphs) lose fine visual detail when encoding observations and lack principled mechanisms to retrieve and integrate memories for multi-hop spatial reasoning about location queries.
motivation: Robots need to answer natural-language location queries (e.g. 'nearest coffee shop southwest of here') by recalling past observations and reasoning spatially, like humans using a cognitive map. Recent work shows explicit cognitive maps improve MLLM spatial reasoning, motivating an agent that builds a task-specific cognitive map from retrieved memories.
key_idea: An LLM agent stores raw images plus positions and captions as semantic-spatial memories, then uses semantic retrieval, spatial-range retrieval and a memory-integration tool that builds a query-specific cognitive map for a VLM to infer the target location.
insight: Keeping raw images for VLM verification recovers details lost in captions (removing raw image memory drops Basic from 67.8 to 60.7 and average from 63.9 to 58.5). The cognitive-map integration is what helps global route-based queries (removing it drops Global from 62.2 to 49.6, near baseline), and spatial-range retrieval adds a further gain (average 61.7 without it vs 63.9).
method: Memory building: per t-second (3 s) video clip, a VLM caption (Qwen2.5-VL-7B or VILA1.5-13B) is embedded with mxbai-embed-large-v1; four evenly spaced frames are concatenated into one raw image; caption, embedding, image and robot position are stored as one entry in Milvus.

Semantic-Similarity Retrieval (mandatory tool): the LLM extracts the target object text, embeds it, retrieves top-k entries, then GPT-4o inspects the raw images to verify the object and produces a refined caption (coarse-to-fine).

Spatial-Range Retrieval: the LLM picks an anchor position and a radius (e.g. 3 m around a water dispenser, 50 m around a supermarket) to retrieve nearby memories; the LLM filters top-k by caption, then the VLM checks the original images.

Memory-Integration: the LLM identifies landmarks (start, end, candidates, directional indicators); a topological map is built from stored positions, Dijkstra gives paths between landmarks, and rule-based or generative rendering yields a query-specific cognitive map that a VLM uses to infer the location.
Agent inference: a LangChain GPT-4o agent iteratively calls tools (only SSR mandatory) until an answer (x,y) or the step limit is reached.
SpaceLocQA benchmark: 6 handheld campus videos (68 min), 15 queries each of basic/local/global type per sequence (270 total), poses from Fast-LIO2, labeled by three experts with cross-validation.
Real-world deployment: offline memory loaded on an AgileX Scout Mini; Dijkstra waypoints, Fast-LIO pose from Livox Mid-360, NeuPan for local navigation.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, LLM agent and VLM verifier); Qwen2.5-VL-7B / VILA1.5-13B for captioning; mxbai-embed-large-v1 for embeddings
setting.observation: egocentric video (RGB) with robot positions from LiDAR odometry (Fast-LIO)
setting.action_space: outputs a 2D (x,y) target coordinate; real robot navigates via Dijkstra waypoints and NeuPan
setting.simulator: real world only (offline recorded videos; no simulator)
setting.privileged: none (poses from Fast-LIO2 for memory positions; query answered from stored memory)

numbers.extra: success = predicted position within 15 m of ground truth; average of 3 runs; mean over 6 sequences

numbers_note: SpaceLocQA and NaVQA are not in the canonical list; split names are approximated as test since the paper defines no train/val split.
results: Meta-Memory beats ReMEmbR, Embodied-RAG and human volunteers on SpaceLocQA: 67.8 basic (vs 58.5), 61.8 local (vs 57.8), 62.2 global (vs 49.3 human, 46.3 ReMEmbR). On NaVQA it reaches a mean position error of 21.7 m vs 28.5 m for ReMEmbR.
limitations: LLM hallucination can cause erroneous reasoning
Designed for static environments; cannot handle dynamic scenes or memory updates
Retrieval relies on text embedding models; relies on GPT-4o API and the new benchmark is small (270 queries, 6 sequences, one campus)
